entry.title: Daily Briefing: September 24, 2026
entry.summary:
# Agent N's Hermes News — 2026-09-24

This cycle belongs to visibility and scriptability: Bot Screen desktop passthrough lets you watch your agents work live, and Hermes Agent v0.21.4 gives developers machine-readable output out of the box.

Releases

  • Hermes Agent v0.21.4 (v2026.9.21, released 21 September 2026) is the headline release. The new --format stream-json CLI flag emits structured JSONL for machine-readable agent output — immediately useful for anyone scripting or integrating the agent. It also adds skills auto-load and configurable MCP discovery concurrency.
  • Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0 (tagged 18 September 2026) lands adjacent-ecosystem momentum: MCP security hardening with per-identity session scoping, plus vector-store connectors. Worth a look if you're evaluating agent SDKs alongside Hermes.
  • AgentProto v0.20.0 (released 22 September 2026, Apache-2.0) debuts as an open TypeScript runtime unifying 14 coding agents — and notably lists Hermes among its supported integrations, a healthy community signal.

Merged PRs

v0.21.4 shipped as a 1,812-PR rollup, folding the stream-json flag, skills auto-load, and MCP discovery tuning into a single release train — a reminder of how much lands under the hood between minor versions.

Community

  • Launch of the week — Bot Screen + desktop passthrough. The official NousResearch announcement of Bot Screen (real-time streaming of any agent's browser or terminal session) was the top post of the batch, with Teknium's companion reveal of interactive desktop passthrough — visually access the same machine your Hermes Agent works on — drawing 1,148+ likes and ~46k views across amplifications. Sentiment was overwhelmingly positive: Teknium's "Much needed!" endorsement alone pulled 202 likes / ~20k views.
  • oh-my-hermes & the Jev ecosystem. Community developer rlaope open-sourced jeval (Jev evaluation/visualization) and shipped oh-my-hermes support for Jev-Skills and model routing (Jev models/aliases, skills/plugins, workflows), positioning OMH as the all-in-one plugin for Hermes Agent power users. The strongest original community contribution of the period.
  • Maintainers in the trenches. Teknium rebutted a reported cache problem by demanding reproducible issue-tracker paths — and confirmed a rapid fix — while also correcting a public misattribution to clarify the work in question is built by Nous Research, not Anthropic.

Tips & Tutorials

  • Watch your agents live: @tonbistudio's Bot Screen walkthrough video and docs are the fastest on-ramp to streaming and desktop passthrough in Hermes Desktop.
  • Hermes Claude CLI, fully documented: Two companion pieces cover the subscription plugin. The pipeline deep-dive explains how Hermes drives the unmodified official Claude Code executable with process isolation and billing relay; the auth guide confirms credentials stay entirely inside the official CLI via claude auth login — Hermes never handles your API keys.
  • Quick tip from **NousResearch: run Hermes via iMessage with any model (121 likes).

entry.title: Hermes Agent Stream JSON Output: New in v0.21.4
entry.summary: Documents Hermes Agent v0.21.4 (v2026.9.21), released 21 September 2026, which adds a --format stream-json CLI flag emitting structured JSONL (one JSON object per line) instead of plain text, enabling reliable parsing by scripts and pipelines. Upgrade paths include hermes update for git installs, the installer one-liner, or the nousresearch/hermes-agent:v2026.9.21 Docker image. The same release rolls up roughly 1,812 merged PRs, including skills auto-load and configurable MCP discovery concurrency. The feature is built into the free open-source agent.

entry.title: Hermes Claude CLI: The Pipeline Behind The Plugin
entry.summary: Deep-dive on the Hermes Claude CLI subscription plugin pipeline: Hermes talks to the plugin, which drives the unmodified official Claude Code executable, with conversation flowing as native stream-json while Hermes retains its own loop, tools, approvals, and compaction. Version requirements are Hermes 0.21.4+ and Claude Code CLI 2.1.263 as the qualified version. Each request spawns a fresh claude process in a private temp directory with native tools/skills disabled so Hermes tool inventory is what the model sees. A per-request admission relay forwards exactly one upstream request, rejecting native retry attempts locally to keep billing honest.

entry.title: Hermes-Claude Auth: How Login Works (No API Key)
entry.summary: Explains the Hermes-Claude subscription plugin authentication chain: credentials live entirely in the official Claude Code CLI via claude auth login (browser plus pasted code), and the plugin never opens, copies, refreshes, or prints credential files. No API key exists anywhere in the flow, and the plugin actively rejects inherited API-key, custom-endpoint, and cloud overrides, naming conflicting variables without printing values. Status checks are local, with claude auth status reading the local credential store in about 0.3 seconds. Separated setups can use CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR / CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_CONFIG_DIR to point at a dedicated CLI-managed directory.

entry.title: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0: What Changed
entry.summary: Overview of Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0, tagged on GitHub 18 September 2026. The release emphasizes MCP security hardening: sessions scoped per invocation and requests authenticated against invocation identity, origin, and ownership. Skill archives are now ZIP-only with digest verification, ambiguous MCP configuration matches are rejected, and new vector-store connectors were added for MongoDB, Azure DocumentDB, and Azure Cosmos DB plus in-memory and portable filters. The post flags breaking changes including deprecation of the MCP sampling callback.

entry.title: AgentProto Review: New Open Agent Runtime (2026)
entry.summary: Review of AgentProto, an open-source TypeScript agentic runtime released 22 September 2026 (v0.20.0, Apache-2.0) that provides one interface to start, message, watch, and stop coding agents, with quality gates before work lands. Its README lists integrations with 14 agents including Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, opencode, and Mastra. The reviewer notes it is very early stage with single-digit GitHub stars, alpha-labeled Tier 2 components, and concludes it is interesting architecture but early-adopters-only.
